the suspension of a guaranteed liberty in a time of war or grave public danger
a statutory provision that seeks to bar courts from inquiring into an official act
a proclaimed condition of danger to the nation that allows some guarantees to be suspended temporarily
items.s: Public emergency: a proclaimed condition of danger to the nation that allows some guarantees to be suspended temporarily. The other options describe Ouster clause, Reasonable justification, Derogation.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Joint account.
o: the arrangement under which a state holds and shares the funds due to its councils
the rule that an area receives a share of revenue from the resource extracted within it
the division of taxing and spending authority between the centre and the component units
the portion of the central pool due to the third tier, usually paid through the states
items.s: Joint account: the arrangement under which a state holds and shares the funds due to its councils. The other options describe Fiscal federalism, Derivation principle, Local government allocation.

items.q: The correct meaning of Limitation clause is
o: a provision allowing a law to restrict a guaranteed liberty in a stated manner and to a stated extent
the test that a restriction must be defensible in a free and open community, not merely convenient for the state
the suspension of a guaranteed liberty in a time of war or grave public danger
an entitlement that may never be suspended, even during a declared emergency
items.s: Limitation clause: a provision allowing a law to restrict a guaranteed liberty in a stated manner and to a stated extent. The other options describe Non-derogable guarantee, Derogation, Reasonable justification.

items.q: In this course, Transition programme refers to
o: the timetable by which a military administration hands power back to elected civilians
the overthrow of a civilian administration by armed forces, an event that has interrupted constitutional rule in Nigeria
the setting aside of the fundamental law, which military regimes did by decree
the sudden seizure of authority by force outside the settled constitutional order
items.s: Transition programme: the timetable by which a military administration hands power back to elected civilians. The other options describe Suspension of the constitution, Military intervention, Coup d'etat.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Entrenched provision.
o: the very large vote in each house needed to alter the most protected items of the fundamental law
a clause whose alteration demands a more exacting procedure than ordinary legislation
a change to the area or number of component states, requiring the heaviest majorities and local approval
a formal change to the text of the supreme law made by the procedure it lays down
items.s: Entrenched provision: a clause whose alteration demands a more exacting procedure than ordinary legislation. The other options describe Alteration of boundaries, Amendment, Four-fifths majority.

items.q: “a person or body allowed to assist the court with argument although not a party to the case” is the definition of
o: Originating motion
Amicus curiae
Enforcement Procedure Rules
Public interest litigation
items.s: Amicus curiae is a person or body allowed to assist the court with argument although not a party to the case.

items.q: The correct meaning of Deprivation of citizenship is
o: the holding of the status of two states at the same time
the removal of national status by the President, allowed only on grounds such as fraud or disloyalty
the claim to belong to a community native to a place, used locally as a criterion for entitlements
a person who is not a national of the state in which he is present
items.s: Deprivation of citizenship: the removal of national status by the President, allowed only on grounds such as fraud or disloyalty. The other options describe Indigeneship, Alien, Dual nationality.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Macpherson Constitution?
o: the 1946 instrument that divided the country into Northern, Western and Eastern Regions
the 1951 instrument that gave each region a house of assembly and created a central council of ministers
the 1979 instrument that created an executive President, a bicameral legislature and a council of states
the 1963 instrument that replaced the monarch as head of state with an indigenous President
items.s: Macpherson Constitution: the 1951 instrument that gave each region a house of assembly and created a central council of ministers. The other options describe Republican Constitution, Presidential Constitution, Richards Constitution.

items.q: Election petition may be defined as
o: the procedure by which registered voters of an area remove their representative before his term ends
the method by which a voter marks a choice privately so that no other person can know it
the special proceeding by which the outcome of a contest is challenged before a tribunal
the defined area whose registered residents choose a representative
items.s: Election petition: the special proceeding by which the outcome of a contest is challenged before a tribunal. The other options describe Recall, Constituency, Secret ballot.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Military intervention?
o: the overthrow of a civilian administration by armed forces, an event that has interrupted constitutional rule in Nigeria
the setting aside of the fundamental law, which military regimes did by decree
the timetable by which a military administration hands power back to elected civilians
the proclamation by the President that a condition of danger exists, published and laid before the legislature
items.s: Military intervention: the overthrow of a civilian administration by armed forces, an event that has interrupted constitutional rule in Nigeria. The other options describe State of emergency, Transition programme, Suspension of the constitution.

items.q: The correct meaning of Primaries is
o: the formal recognition of a group by the electoral body as qualified to sponsor candidates
the endorsement of a candidate by a recognised group, without which a nomination fails
the published programme of policies that a group offers to the electorate
the internal contest by which a group selects the candidate it will sponsor
items.s: Primaries: the internal contest by which a group selects the candidate it will sponsor. The other options describe Sponsorship, Manifesto, Party registration.

items.q: In this course, Revenue Mobilisation Allocation and Fiscal Commission refers to
o: the central pool into which most national revenue is paid before it is shared among the tiers
the share of the central pool distributed to each tier under the sharing formula
the portion of the central pool due to the third tier, usually paid through the states
the body that advises on the formula for sharing the central pool
items.s: Revenue Mobilisation Allocation and Fiscal Commission: the body that advises on the formula for sharing the central pool. The other options describe Local government allocation, Statutory allocation, Federation Account.

items.q: Select the statement that correctly explains Presidential Constitution.
o: the 1922 instrument that first allowed a few elected members into the Nigerian Legislative Council
the practice of filling some seats in a legislature by popular vote instead of nomination
the 1979 instrument that created an executive President, a bicameral legislature and a council of states
the 1951 instrument that gave each region a house of assembly and created a central council of ministers
items.s: Presidential Constitution: the 1979 instrument that created an executive President, a bicameral legislature and a council of states. The other options describe Macpherson Constitution, Elective principle, Clifford Constitution.

items.q: In this course, Coup d'etat refers to
o: the sudden seizure of authority by force outside the settled constitutional order
the timetable by which a military administration hands power back to elected civilians
the setting aside of the fundamental law, which military regimes did by decree
the formal public notice by which the executive announces a condition of danger
items.s: Coup d'etat: the sudden seizure of authority by force outside the settled constitutional order. The other options describe Proclamation, Transition programme, Suspension of the constitution.

items.q: Which concept is defined by this statement? “the liberty to gather peacefully and to form or join bodies such as trade unions and political groups”
o: Fundamental right
Freedom of association
Dignity of the human person
Freedom of expression
items.s: Freedom of association is the liberty to gather peacefully and to form or join bodies such as trade unions and political groups.
